description.description:
Description explains what the command does. This is the long-form text
shown in the TUI's right-hand pane, so it can run to several paragraphs.

params.description:
Params are the parameters this command accepts. They are validated and
type-coerced before any step runs, then substituted into the steps.

steps.description:
Steps are run in order, each as its own process. The command stops at
the first step that exits non-zero and reports that exit code. A step
may itself be a parallel group, for running several services together.

output.description:
Output describes what the command produces: what it writes to stdout,
what files it leaves behind, what a reader should expect to see. It is
documentation only and noodge never verifies it.

env.description: Env is set for this command's steps, merged over the file-level env.

cwd.description:
Cwd is the working directory for this command's steps, relative to the
directory holding the noodge.yaml. Defaults to that directory.

aliases.description: Aliases are alternative names this command can be invoked by.

hidden.description:
Hidden keeps the command out of the TUI list and out of tab completion.
It remains runnable by name. Use it for internal or CI-only commands.

confirm.description:
Confirm asks the user to confirm before this command runs. Write true for
a default prompt, or a string to use as the prompt itself. Omit it, or
write false, to run without asking. Use it for destructive or
irreversible commands. Confirmation is skipped by --yes and by --dry-run,
and without a terminal to ask at the command refuses unless --yes is given.

shell.description: Shell overrides the interpreter for this command's string steps.

Command.description: Command is one runnable, documented entry in a noodge.yaml.

Commands.description: The runnable commands, keyed by the name you type after `noodge`.

Confirm.title: Confirm
Confirm.description: Ask before the command runs. true asks with a default prompt; a string asks with that prompt. Omitted or false runs without asking. Meant for destructive or irreversible commands.

prefix.description:
Prefix is the family this describes: the part of a command name before
its first colon. For "dev:api" and "dev:worker" the prefix is "dev".

title.description:
Title is the heading shown above the family in the browser. Defaults to
the prefix itself when omitted.

description.description:
Description is the line or two shown when the family's heading is
highlighted. Use it for what the banner comments in a long file would
have said.

Group.description: Group documents a family of commands in the browser: every command whose name begins with Prefix followed by a colon, plus a command named exactly Prefix.

name.description:
Name is the template variable this parameter fills. A step referring to
{{host}} or {{flag host}} is referring to the parameter named "host".

flag.description:
Flag is how the parameter is typed on the noodge command line, written
in full including the leading dashes, for example "--host". It must use
two dashes; single-dash long flags cannot be expressed.

This is independent of how the flag reaches the wrapped tool. A step is
free to write "-host {{host}}" or "/p:Host={{host}}" instead.

short.description:
Short is an optional single-character shorthand, written with one dash,
for example "-c".

type.description: Type is the value's type. Defaults to string.

description.description:
Description explains what the parameter controls. Shown beside the
field in the TUI and in the command's help text.

required.description: Required refuses to run the command unless the parameter is given.

default.description:
Default is used when the parameter is not supplied. A parameter with a
default is never unset, so {{flag x}} always expands for it.

values.description:
Values is the list of allowed values for an enum parameter. It also
supplies the candidates for tab completion.

pattern.description:
Pattern is an optional regular expression the value must match. It is
checked before the value is substituted into any step.

Param.description: Param is one parameter a command accepts.

parallel.description: Things to start at once, keyed by a name that labels their output. The group ends when one fails or all of them finish.

prefix.description: Label each output line with the entry it came from. On by default. Labelling requires capturing the output through a pipe, which makes most programs turn their colours off; set this to false to let them write straight to the terminal instead.

Step.title: Step
Step.description: One entry in the sequence. A string is run through a shell; a list of arguments is executed directly with no shell; a parallel group starts its entries at once.

version.description: Version is the config format version. Currently always 1.

name.description: Name is a human-readable name for the project, shown in the TUI header.

shell.description:
Shell overrides the interpreter used to run string steps. Defaults to
"cmd /c" on Windows and "sh -c" everywhere else. A per-command shell
takes precedence over this.

env.description:
Env is applied to every command in this file. A command's own env is
merged over the top, so a command can override a single variable
without restating the rest.

groups.description:
Groups give the command families a heading and a short description in the
browser. A command belongs to the family named by the part of its name
before the first colon, so "dev:api" and "dev:worker" are both in the
"dev" family. Declaring a family here is optional — families are shown
either way, headed by the bare prefix; this only adds a readable title
and a line of explanation.

commands.description:
Commands are the runnable commands, kept in the order they appear in
the file so the TUI can list them the way they were written.

title: noodge.yaml
description: Configuration for noodge, a documented, discoverable task runner.
